overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the March 17 litigation-strategy executive session under Purpose 3 was justified, and no individual notice was required, though Purpose 7 was not validly invoked.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session on March 17 for an improper purpose (litigation strategy, Purpose 3) where no litigation was actually threatened.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board members reasonably believed that litigation was imminently threatened, based on advice of counsel, we find that they did not violate the Open Meeting Law by entering into executive session under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to give him individual notice that he would be the subject of the executive session discussion and an opportunity to request an open session.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, because Purpose 3 does not require notice to specific individuals, the Board did not violate the law by not providing Mr. Ferguson with individual advance notice of the executive session.

allegations.summary: The Board also cited Purpose 7 (compliance with law) for the executive session without identifying any enabling law requiring confidentiality; the AG reviewed this citation.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board failed to identify a law that required confidentiality, we cannot find that Purpose 7 was a valid reason to enter into executive session
